# @contractkit/explorer-ui

> The HTML renderer behind ContractKit's API explorer. Pure functions that turn resolved contract
> and operation data into HTML strings — no DOM, no framework, no bundler. Themable entirely
> through CSS custom properties.

Used by the ContractKit VS Code extension to render its explorer webview. Install it directly only
if you are building your own explorer surface; it is not part of a normal `contractkit` build and is
not a codegen plugin.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @contractkit/explorer-ui
```

## Use

```typescript
import { renderApp, type PreviewData } from '@contractkit/explorer-ui';

const html: string = renderApp(data);   // data: PreviewData
```

`renderApp` is the whole-page entry point: sidebar, overview, every operation, every model. Compose
a narrower surface from the individual renderers instead:

| Export | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| `renderApp(data)` | The full explorer page |
| `renderItemPage(...)`, `listSelections`, `operationId`, `modelId` | A single-item page and its selection helpers |
| `renderOperation(op)`, `operationAnchor` | One operation |
| `renderModel(m)`, `renderFieldRows`, `modelAnchor` | One model and its field table |
| `renderType`, `renderSchemaTree` | A type expression; an expanded schema tree |
| `renderTryIt` | The try-it request panel |
| `renderCodeSamples` | Per-language request samples |
| `constraintSummary` | A field's constraints as readable text |
| `renderMarkdown` | Contract descriptions and `#` comments |
| `escapeHtml`, `html`, `raw`, `slug` | The tagged-template helpers the renderers are built from |

Types: `PreviewData`, `PreviewConfigMeta`, `PreviewServer`, `PreviewWarning`, `ResolvedOperation`,
`ResolvedModel`, `ItemSelection`.

## Theming

Output carries `ce-` prefixed class names and reads colours and spacing from CSS custom properties,
so it inherits a host theme (VS Code light/dark, say) without a rebuild. Style it from outside; do
not fork the renderers to change appearance.

## Gotchas

- Every function returns an HTML **string**. Nothing is mounted, no stylesheet is injected, and no
  interactivity is attached — supply the surrounding document, the CSS, and any behaviour yourself.
- Input is *resolved* data (`ResolvedOperation`, `ResolvedModel`), not a raw `@contractkit/core`
  AST. Resolve first.
- `html` and `raw` exist because the renderers escape by default. Interpolating pre-rendered HTML
  through anything other than `raw` will double-escape it; passing untrusted text through `raw`
  defeats the escaping.
